title: Two up is not enough: give the National League a third promotion place

defects.correction: Rochdale finished second in the 2025-26 National League with 106 points, two behind York City.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] The first half of the sentence (York City top with 108 points) is true; only Rochdale's total is wrong. True value: 106 points. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_National_League_play-off_final (final table); also https://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/york-promoted-after-stoppage-time-chaos/231702

defects.correction: Boreham Wood finished fourth in the 2025-26 National League with 90 points; Scunthorpe United finished fifth.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] The sixteen-point gap to Rochdale in the same clause is true (106 against 90); only the league position is wrong. True value: fourth. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_National_League_play-off_final

defects.quote: The final was played in front of 21,740 people
defects.correction: The attendance at the 2026 National League play-off final at Wembley was 17,740.

defects.correction: Boreham Wood's goals in the final were scored by Matt Rush (22') and Abdul Abdulmalik (69'); Zak Brunt did not score.
defects.note: [needs-source] [multi-part] Matt Rush did score the first goal; only the second scorer is wrong. True value: Abdul Abdulmalik, 69'. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_National_League_play-off_final

defects.correction: Rochdale won the penalty shoot-out 3-1 after the final finished 2-2 after extra time.

defects.quote: Teams that lose the play-off final take an average of six years to come back up.
A team that finished second nearly stayed down, which proves that the play-offs are a lottery and should be abolished.
defects.known_rebuttal: One close final does not show that the play-offs are a lottery: Rochdale, the best of the six play-off sides over the season, did win promotion. The argument also confuses two questions. How many clubs go up is separate from how the last place is decided, and a third promotion place can be added while keeping the play-offs. Play-offs keep the season alive for clubs down to seventh place and draw some of the division's biggest crowds, such as the 13,814 at Carlisle's semi-final, so abolishing them would cost the league interest and income.
